title: CYBRIK W1 investigation lifecycle and transport proposal v1
description: Additive packet for create/status/checkpoint/cancel/bundle-read REST mapping and Cyber AI lifecycle events. It reuses the accepted W0-I01 artifact packet without changing its bytes or lifecycle, leaves W2-D as the sole existing inference-path owner, and treats W2-F only as an identity/delegation seam in front of SOC-to-Cyber-AI inference operations — never as Fabric tool-execution authority. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION v0.1.0 packet (W1-C2; not stable v1/GA) — NOT IMPLEMENTED, CI NOT WIRED. W1-REC-3/4 accepts json-schema/cybrik.investigation-bundle.strict-compatible.v1.schema.json v0.1.1 and makes it authoritative for new bundle-read responses while preserving accepted cybrik.investigation-bundle.v1 v0.1.0 as immutable supported legacy read/replay input with byte-unchanged SHA-256 evidence. Consumer migration remains separately gated by W1-REC-5.

supersession_mapping.compatibility: Semantic shape is preserved. The accepted v0.1.0 is and remains fully JSON Schema 2020-12 conformant; nothing in it is spec-invalid and nothing in it is being repaired. Its generated_by.allOf[1] is the bare subschema {"required":["tenant_id"]}, which the 2020-12 specification permits and which is rejected only by Ajv's optional strict-mode house style (strictRequired/strictTypes), never by the specification itself. The accepted v0.1.1 successor selected by W1-REC-3/4 changes only lifecycle metadata plus generated_by.allOf[1], where it adds an explicit "type": "object" and a local "properties": {"tenant_id": {"$ref": "cybrik.common-defs.v1.schema.json#/$defs/tenantId"}} subschema. That tenant_id subschema is newly written into allOf[1] — it was not present there before — and it is semantically redundant, because allOf[0]'s actor $ref already constrains tenant_id to the identical tenantId primitive. The successor therefore narrows, widens, and removes nothing; it only satisfies the stricter Ajv strict-mode house style.

This binding creates no product runtime, server, bus, Fabric, deployment, release, or automatic consumer-migration authority; consumer migration remains separately gated by W1-REC-5.

state_machine.note: run_status is a transport/orchestrator view, not a redefinition of the accepted investigation record status.

runtime_invariants.statement: Authoritative tenant and actor derive from authenticated identity; any body/actor/credential tenant mismatch is rejected.
Authoritative org scope derives from identity plus policy; advisory org_scope never expands visibility and a mismatch is rejected.
Idempotency is scoped to authenticated principal plus key plus normalized body. Same triple returns the same result; same principal/key with different content returns idempotency_conflict.
Cancellation is compare-and-set on expected_version. A stale version loses; exactly one state transition wins a cancellation/checkpoint/completion race.
Terminal attempts are immutable. Late cancellation/checkpoints return or observe current truth and never rewrite state, drop checkpoints, or discard Fabric receipts.
Checkpoint sequence is strictly increasing per attempt. Retry creates a fresh attempt_id linked to the prior attempt and starts sequence at one; no prior attempt is mutated.
Status, checkpoint, event, and bundle-read markings never downgrade authoritative input/artifact markings on either classification or TLP axis.

Unknown and unauthorized investigation ids are indistinguishable in HTTP class, JSON shape, sanitized message policy, and timing policy; no existence, owner, tenant, org, grant, or policy detail leaks. The positive not-found plus negative existence-leak fixtures verify only the static shape/message/no-target-identifier portion; timing indistinguishability remains an explicit runtime-only obligation and is not claimed as fixture-verified.

authority_invariants: No schema permits capability, delegation, approval, tool, MCP, action, credential, provider, or endpoint authority fields.
W2-F inference delegation is never treated as Fabric tool-execution authority.
Claims/model output remain advisory and cannot transition lifecycle state or authorize an action.
Any future Cyber AI tool use must invoke the separate Fabric-owned contract under its own policy, approval, receipt, and credential boundaries.

x-cybrik-packet-integrity.file_digest_rule: Every member except this manifest is digested as the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact on-disk UTF-8 bytes of '<path_root><file>'.
x-cybrik-packet-integrity.self_digest_rule: This manifest's own member digest is deliberately NOT taken over its on-disk bytes. It is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 encoding of JSON.stringify(this manifest parsed as JSON with the top-level 'x-cybrik-packet-integrity' key removed). Because the hashed input excludes the integrity block, no digest input ever contains a digest, which is what makes the self entry and the aggregate below non-circular and independently reproducible. Consequence, stated deliberately: for this one member the digest pins the JSON value, not the on-disk byte formatting.
x-cybrik-packet-integrity.aggregate_algorithm: Sort all 30 member entries ascending by 'file' using JavaScript default string comparison, render each entry as the line '<sha256>  <file>' (two spaces), join the lines with a single '\n' and no trailing newline, then take the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 encoding of that string. The aggregate consumes only the 30 member digests, so it never depends on its own value.
